moa.t: Replaces potassium, needed for membrane potential and cardiac conduction

items.t: Potassium chloride, oral, 600 mg, 1–2 tablets 8 hourly. · Each 600 mg potassium chloride tablet contains 8 mmol of potassium chloride.
Potassium chloride, oral, 1 200 mg (2 tablets) 8 hourly. · Each 600 mg potassium chloride tablet contains 8 mmol of potassium chloride.
Potassium chloride, IV by peripheral line, 40 mmol in 1 L of 0.9% or 0.45% sodium chloride, mixed thoroughly. · Administer over 3 hours, or up to a maximum rate of 20 mmol per

dosing.h: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) and Hyperosmolar Hyperglycaemic State (HHS)

items.t: Potassium chloride, IV, added to 1 L of fluid. o potassium <3.5 mmol/L: add 40 mmol (2 ampoules). o potassium 3.5–5.5 mmol/L: add 20 mmol (1 ampoule).
Potassium chloride, IV, 20 mmol (1 ampoule) added to 1 L of fluid as soon as the patient has established adequate urinary output.
Potassium chloride, IV, 20 to 40 mmol/L in sodium chloride, 0.9%. · Maximum rate of infusion: 20 mmol/hour.

Potassium chloride, IV, diluted in 1 L sodium chloride 0.9%. · Rapid infusion of potassium chloride can cause fatal dysrhythmias. · Infusion rates > 20 mmol/hour are very irritating to peripheral veins.
Potassium chloride, oral, 8 hourly. · If < 6 months: 125 mg. · If > 6 months: 250 mg.

dosing.h: Congenital Heart Disease with Left to Right Shunt

items.t: Supplement with potassium chloride, oral, 25–50 mg/kg/dose 8–12 hourly.
Potassium chloride (100 mg/ml), oral, 75–225 mg/kg/day (1–3 mmol/kg/day or 0.75–2.25 ml/kg/day) in divided doses. · Monitor serum potassium.

cautions.t: Never give undiluted or as a bolus
Maximum rate and concentration per protocol
Correct magnesium if hypokalaemia is refractory

adverse_effects.t: Hyperkalaemia, arrhythmias, cardiac arrest with rapid IV, phlebitis, GI ulceration with oral

monitoring.t: Potassium, ECG at higher rates, urine output
